title: Counterfactual Fairness in Text Classification through Robustness
findings: The baseline toxicity classifier exhibited significant bias based on religious identity tokens, assigning a toxicity score of 0.46 to 'Some people are Muslim' versus only 0.04 to 'Some people are Christian'. The proposed Counterfactual Logit Pairing (CLP) method successfully mitigated this bias, resulting in nearly identical scores (0.14 for Muslim, 0.14 for Christian) for the same sentences.

measurement_description: Bias in toxicity prediction scores when swapping religious identity tokens (e.g., 'Jewish', 'Muslim', 'Christian') within otherwise identical sentences. The paper measures this using a metric called Counterfactual Token Fairness (CTF).
